\begin{exercise} \end{exercise} 1. ch5:5-11

Recall the groups $E(n)$, $O(n+1)$, and $O^+(n,1)$ defined in Chapter 3, which act isometrically on the model Riemannian manifolds $(\mathbb {R}^n, \overline{g})$, $(S^n(R), \overline{g}_R)$, and $(\mathbb {H}^n(R), \overline{g}_R)$, respectively.

  1. Show that

    \[ \operatorname {Iso}(\mathbb {R}^n,\overline{g}) = E(n), \qquad \operatorname {Iso}(S^n(R),\overline{g}_R) = O(n+1), \qquad \operatorname {Iso}(\mathbb {H}^n(R),\overline{g}_R) = O^+(n,1). \]

  2. Show that in each case, for each point $p$ in $\mathbb {R}^n$, $S^n(R)$, or $\mathbb {H}^n(R)$, the isotropy group at $p$ is a subgroup isomorphic to $O(n)$.

  3. Strengthen the result above by showing that if $(M,g)$ is one of the Riemannian manifolds $(\mathbb {R}^n,\overline{g})$, $(S^n(R),\overline{g}_R)$, or $(\mathbb {H}^n(R),\overline{g}_R)$, $U$ is a connected open subset of $M$, and $\varphi : U \to M$ is a local isometry, then $\varphi $ is the restriction to $U$ of an element of $\operatorname {Iso}(M,g)$.

(Used on pp. 57, 58, 67, 348, 349.) \end{exercise}
